tools.name: explain_stock
tools.description: Use this when the user asks about one company or ticker in general: 'tell me about X', 'what does X do', 'how is X doing', 'explain X stock', its price, chart or business. Shows invest-like's stock page in a card: price and one-year chart, one plain sentence, four checks with the numbers behind them (is it profitable, growing, fairly priced, carrying debt), strengths, risks, what to watch, the halal result, how many of seven investors' published rulebooks it meets, and invest-like's stored AI analysis when one exists. Covers 21,000+ stocks in 60+ countries, refreshed daily. For 'is X a good buy' or 'is X undervalued' use check_value instead.

stock.description: Ticker or company name, e.g. 'NVDA', 'Coca-Cola' or 'SAP.DE'

tools.name: check_value
tools.description: Use this when the user asks whether a stock is a good buy, a good investment, worth buying, undervalued, overvalued, cheap, expensive, or worth it at today's price. Shows invest-like's answer to 'Is it undervalued?' from a fixed, published rule, with the numbers behind it (P/E against its peers, price to free cash flow, earnings yield, sales growth), short answers on financial health, moat and dividend safety, and, when a stored AI analysis exists, what today's price expects. It never says buy or sell: use it to explain what the price assumes.

stock.description: Ticker or company name, e.g. 'NVDA', 'Coca-Cola' or 'SAP.DE'

tools.name: compare_stocks
tools.description: Use this when the user names 2 to 4 stocks and asks which is better, to compare them, or writes 'X or Y' / 'X vs Y' (e.g. 'Visa or Mastercard?', 'Apple vs Microsoft'). Shows them side by side: the four plain checks (profit, growth, price, debt), sales growth, net margin, return on capital, P/E, debt, dividend, one-year price change and market value, with the stronger figure marked, plus the halal result and the rulebooks met.

tools.name: score_portfolio
tools.description: Use this when the user shares the stocks or funds they own (a portfolio, holdings, 'my stocks', a broker list) and wants to know how it looks, a score, or what to watch. Takes up to 60 holdings, each a ticker or company name with optional shares or money amount. Returns invest-like's portfolio score from 0 to 100 (quality, value, growth, safety, spread), a plain read of the whole portfolio, its weights, how its P/E, margin, growth and dividend compare with the 500 largest US companies, one strength and one thing to watch. ETFs such as VOO or VWCE are supported. No login or personal data needed.

shares.description: Number of shares, if the user gave it

amount.description: Money in this holding, in the portfolio currency, if the user gave it

currency.description: Currency of the amounts and the report (default USD)

halal.description: true when the user cares whether the holdings are halal

tools.name: find_stocks
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for stock ideas or a list by a rule: stocks that meet an investor's published rules (rulebook: buffett (Warren Buffett), munger (Charlie Munger), graham (Benjamin Graham), fisher (Philip Fisher), lynch (Peter Lynch), greenblatt (Joel Greenblatt), smith (Terry Smith)), one of invest-like's published daily lists (list), or number filters such as P/E below 15, net margin above 20%, dividend yield above 3%, sales growth above 10%, with an optional sector, country and halal-only. Use exactly one of rulebook, list or filters. Lists come only from invest-like's data, never from memory. Results are screen results, not recommendations.

rulebook.description: Stocks that meet this investor's published rules, e.g. 'graham' for 'stocks that pass Benjamin Graham's rules'

list.description: One of invest-like's published lists: strongest-moat, highest-roic, cheapest-pe, cheapest-peg, highest-fcf-yield, safest-dividend, lowest-debt, highest-gross-margin, highest-buyback-yield, halal-top-picks, magic-formula-top-30, consistent-compounders

value.description: Percent metrics in percent (20 = 20%), market value in USD, P/E and net debt / EBITDA as plain numbers

country.description: Two-letter country code, e.g. US, DE, GB

halal_only.description: Only stocks that pass the halal screen

sort.description: For filters: the figure to sort by (default market value)

tools.name: check_rulebook
tools.description: Use this when the user asks whether a stock fits a famous investor's style or rules ('would Buffett like X', 'does X pass Graham's rules', 'Lynch checklist for X'). Shows how the company does against seven investors' published rulebooks as applied by invest-like (Warren Buffett, Charlie Munger, Benjamin Graham, Philip Fisher, Peter Lynch, Joel Greenblatt, Terry Smith): a fit from 0 to 100 for each, and, for one named investor, each rule with the company's real value and whether it is met. These are published rules applied by invest-like, never the investor's own opinion of the stock.

stock.description: Ticker or company name, e.g. 'NVDA', 'Coca-Cola' or 'SAP.DE'

investor.description: Show this investor's rules one by one

tools.name: check_halal
tools.description: Use this when the user asks whether one or more stocks are halal, Shariah-compliant or permissible for a Muslim investor. Takes 1 to 10 tickers or company names and shows invest-like's AAOIFI-based screen for each: halal, questionable or not halal, the reason in plain words, the business test and interest-bearing debt as a share of market value. A screen, not a fatwa.
